reason: No port. A duplicate is a second `var` binding of the same name in the same function scope (var hoists through blocks, not through nested functions). Name identity across two declarations needs shared metavariables across relations, and the hoisting scope needs a scope graph. Metavariable identity works only within one pattern. Such a pattern anchors on the enclosing node, and contextual selectors drop the identity: `{context: "var $A = $V, $A = $W", selector: "variable_declarator"}` matches every declarator.

evidence.why: `var duplicated = null;` duplicates the line 10 declarator in the same method and is anchored on its own name. No single-node pattern can see line 10
`var notDuplicated = 345;` repeats a line 9 name inside an arrow function, which is a new var scope, so it is not a failure. Needs function-scope boundaries
`var d = 2` inside an if-block duplicates the function-level `let d`. Hoisting crosses the block, and an any-ancestor relation cannot bind the name
